title: Investigate: GET /api/portfolio's first load is very slow; can IBKR speed it up when connected?
description:
User-reported performance issue: the Portfolio page's first load is 'very very slow'. Investigated the current implementation before writing this task (read, not profiled live -- this task's first job is to actually measure, not assume):

`GET /api/portfolio` (`get_portfolio` in `app/api/routers/portfolio.py`) currently does, for a portfolio of N held positions in swing mode (the default, and almost certainly what the reporting user has active): (1) `enrich_positions_with_price` fetches each position's current price via the swing `DataProvider` (yfinance-primary/Stooq-fallback behind a SQLite cache) -- whether this loop is sequential or already concurrent needs checking directly, not assumed; (2) a separate `for e in enriched` loop then calls `_compute_position_signal`, which for EVERY position in swing mode makes ANOTHER blocking `provider.get_weekly_ohlcv(ticker)` call, sequentially, one position at a time, with no concurrency at all. So a swing-mode portfolio load can be up to ~2N sequential external-provider round trips (cache-cold ones going all the way to a real yfinance/Stooq HTTP request), a plausible root cause for 'very very slow' -- but this needs to be *confirmed* by actually timing it (e.g. add temporary instrumentation, or profile with `cProfile`/manual timestamps around the two loops) before assuming this is the whole story rather than something else (DB query patterns, template config, etc.).

Day-trader mode already has a fully-worked-out concurrent-fetch pattern for exactly this N-tickers problem (`compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently`, `ThreadPoolExecutor`-based, from `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups`) -- that pattern is a strong, low-risk template for speeding up the SWING-mode loops above too, independent of whether IBKR is involved at all (concurrent fetching from the existing swing `DataProvider` itself, no new data source).

The user's own specific ask -- 'can it be faster when using ibkr as much as possible if ibkr is connected' -- is a genuinely bigger, more architecturally sensitive question: it implies substituting or supplementing the swing-mode price/weekly-data fetch with IBKR when available. This directly touches an already-established precedent recorded elsewhere in this codebase's task history: `current_price`/`equity` are documented as 'always swing-provider-derived regardless of the active trading mode' (see `PortfolioResponse.trading_mode`'s own field description and prior day-trader-mode API decisions). Changing that for swing mode specifically -- even only 'when IBKR happens to be connected' -- is a real product/architecture decision, not a pure performance optimization, since it would mean two different portfolios (same account, different moments) could show prices sourced from two different providers depending on IBKR's connection state. This task should investigate whether IBKR even CAN supply what's needed here (IBKR's `IBKRProvider` today only exposes hourly bars/scanner/account-positions -- not a documented daily/weekly OHLCV fetch matching the swing provider's shape) and, if so, treat the swing-vs-IBKR-source question as something to resolve via a `decisions` entry with real weighing of the tradeoff, or escalate as a `questions` entry (state: waiting_input) if it's genuinely the user's call to make -- do not silently start mixing data sources into swing mode's price fields without that explicit resolution.

checklist.step: Measure, don't assume: instrument (or profile) `GET /api/portfolio` against a portfolio with several held positions and a cold cache, and identify where the actual wall-clock time goes -- confirm or correct the hypothesis above (the `enrich_positions_with_price` fetch loop and/or `_compute_position_signal`'s per-position `get_weekly_ohlcv` loop being sequential and provider-round-trip-bound).

If the sequential swing-provider loops are confirmed as the bottleneck: apply concurrent fetching to them, following the same `ThreadPoolExecutor`-based pattern `compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently` already established for the analogous day-trader-mode problem -- this is independent of IBKR and should be safe/low-risk to do regardless of the answer to the IBKR question below. Verify thread-safety against the swing `DataProvider`'s actual implementation (mirroring how the day-trader concurrency work verified `IBKRProvider`'s own mutable-state usage) before assuming it's safe.

Separately investigate whether IBKR can genuinely supply what swing mode's price/weekly-data fetch needs today (check `IBKRProvider`'s actual current capabilities -- hourly bars, account positions, scanner -- against what a daily/weekly-OHLCV-shaped fetch would require) -- if it can't without new IBKR-provider work, say so explicitly and treat that as this task's answer to the user's question (a follow-up task, not silently expanded scope here) rather than attempting a larger IBKR-provider feature under an 'investigation' task's checklist.

If IBKR genuinely could supply swing-mode data faster when connected: record the swing-vs-IBKR-source tradeoff as a `decisions` entry (or a `questions` entry + `waiting_input` state if it's genuinely the user's call, given the precedent tension described in this task's own description) BEFORE implementing anything that changes what `current_price`/`equity`/signal inputs are sourced from in swing mode -- do not silently change this established behavior.

Tests: for whatever concurrency change is made, a genuinely discriminating test proving the concurrent fetch produces the same per-position results as the old sequential loop (not just 'doesn't crash') -- mutation-test it per this codebase's established standard for concurrency-correctness claims.
